extracted.intended_audience: Al Jazeera journalists, editors and media professionals (and the broader journalism community)
extracted.subtask_description: A media organisation's code of ethics setting standards for reporting across broadcast and digital platforms, covering accuracy, fairness, source transparency, treatment of victims, independence, diversity, and support for media freedom.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mission / public-service obligation
rubrics_metrics.description: Inform and empower people with accurate, in-depth and compelling content that upholds the value of truth and elevates the human spirit; be fearless in the pursuit of truth and the voice of the voiceless; act as a bridge between peoples and cultures; promote the right of access to information and respect public liberties and human rights.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the organisational purpose that frames all editorial decisions — content should advance these goals across broadcast and digital platforms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Truth and accuracy
rubrics_metrics.description: Endeavour to get to the truth and report it in our news bulletins, programmes, and stories across broadcast and digital platforms in a manner that leaves no doubt about its validity and accuracy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applies to all reporting and formats; reporting should be thorough enough to remove reasonable doubt about facts and validity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Diversity of viewpoints / impartiality
rubrics_metrics.description: Present diverse points of view and opinions without bias and partiality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure multiple perspectives are represented and avoid favoring one side; applies to both factual coverage and opinion contexts where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correction of errors
rubrics_metrics.description: Acknowledge a mistake when it occurs, promptly correct it and ensure it does not recur.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Errors should be admitted and corrected quickly; organisations should take steps to prevent repeat mistakes (procedural/ editorial learning).

rubrics_metrics.name: Respect for audiences and victims
rubrics_metrics.description: Treat our audiences with due respect and address every issue or story with due attention to present a clear, factual, and accurate picture while giving full consideration to the feelings of victims of crime; war; persecution; and disaster. Also, to respect the relatives of victims as well as individual privacy and public decorum.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Balance the public interest in reporting with sensitivity toward victims, their families, and privacy; present facts clearly while being mindful of possible harm to those affected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Respect for diversity
rubrics_metrics.description: Respect the diversity that characterizes human societies that we recognize are made up of different races, cultures, beliefs, values and which hold unique characteristics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Coverage should reflect and respect cultural, racial, religious and value differences and avoid stereotyped or demeaning portrayals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Core journalistic values and independence
rubrics_metrics.description: Adhere to the journalistic values of honesty, courage, fairness, balance, independence, credibility, and diversity, giving no priority to commercial or political over professional considerations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editorial decisions must privilege professional ethics over commercial pressures or political influence; maintain independence to preserve credibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Responsible competition / restraint on 'scoops'
rubrics_metrics.description: The 'scoop', however important, is not an end in itself, and thereby fair and honest media competition should in no way undermine journalistic values.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not pursue exclusive stories in ways that compromise accuracy, ethics, or other core values; competition must remain ethical.

rubrics_metrics.name: Source transparency and source-rights compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: Observe transparency in dealing with the news and its sources while adhering to the internationally established practices concerning the rights of these sources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be clear with audiences about sourcing; at the same time follow accepted international practices on source protection, consent, and rights (e.g., anonymity where appropriate).

rubrics_metrics.name: Clear separation of news, opinion and analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: Distinguish between news material, opinion, and analysis to avoid the snares of speculation and propaganda.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Label and structure content so audiences can tell factual reporting apart from commentary or interpretive pieces; avoid letting analysis/ opinion masquerade as straight news.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support for media freedom and solidarity with journalists
rubrics_metrics.description: Support all efforts to promote media freedom; stand in solidarity with fellow journalists when they are attacked or harassed because of their commitment to professional values; and cooperate with press institutions and organizations championing media freedom.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The organisation should advocate for press freedom, defend journalists under threat, and collaborate with institutions that protect media rights.
